reference_summary: A 47 s, 16:9 motion-design ad made with Claude Code for a fictional SaaS, "Cast", that turns a skincare brand's reviews into customer personas. The owner watched it as a phone recording of a laptop posted on Instagram with the caption "Claude Cooked". Narrative arc: (1) Thesis hook with three persona characters on screen from frame 0: "Your customers are 3 people. / Not 10,482 reviews. / Three. / And honestly? / You've never met them." (2) Problem: a split-flap board announces "YOUR AD, V1: SPF 50. FOR EVERYONE.", that ad zooms out into a wall of hundreds of identical ads, and a "Scrolled past." stamp lands. (3) Turn: a hard cut to calm, "So we built", three orbs fuse into the logo, and the logo match-moves into the app's sidebar. (4) Demo, as one long take: connect store, live review scan with rolling counters, keywords pulled out of the reviews, a day-to-night time-lapse that stops on a single 2:04 AM review. (5) Personas: particles pour into three empty slots, and each slot opens into a game-style character-select world (Maya, Dev, Rosa) where every trait is a joke acted out by motion. (6) Payoff: three persona ads are built live against a grey generic ad ("In their words. / Not yours.", "Same product. / Three ads."), then bars and a "3x". (7) Meta twist: a VHS pause, and the whole film rewinds to the Claude Code prompt and a code listing that names every effect. (8) CTA: "Comment PROMPTS" is typed into a comment field and a DM notification arrives. The palette is a strict magenta/lime/tangerine on navy, used as a story code. There are two typefaces (a Bricolage-like heavy grotesk plus a mono), real z-space camera work, and everything is locked to a ~161 BPM track with no voice-over and almost no hard cuts. Its premium feel does not come from the colours. It comes from five things: every line is shown as a literal visual metaphor, the same characters persist and react, transitions are continuous object transformations, the micro-world is dense and believable, and the sound is synced frame by frame.

quality_drivers.driver: 1. Every line becomes one literal visual metaphor (the script writes the transitions)
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: 'Not 10,482 reviews' is an endless tunnel of review cards. 'Three.' is the data shattering to reveal the three people. 'You've never met them' becomes pixelated faces, censor bars and a NO DATA stamp. 'Generic ad' is one card that zooms out into a wall of hundreds. 'Reads every label. Twice.' is a magnifier that rewinds its path. 'Not yours.' is the grey card cracking open to reveal the real one underneath. The images carry the meaning, so text and image say the same thing at the same time.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Before writing a line, write the image. Each beat of a tip must be understandable with the sound off and the headline hidden. Examples: 'Coupe dans l'action': Point jumps, the playhead cuts the clip mid-jump and clip B continues the jump. 'Règle des tiers': the viewfinder grid slides in and Point steps onto an intersection. '180°': the axis is a physical line on the floor, Point walks along it, and when the camera crosses it the monitor image flips. 'Hiérarchie typo': three lines, two fall to 40% opacity while one gains weight. 'Lazy-load': the page's images stay as dashed placeholders until Point scrolls. Reject any beat whose image is just a text card with an icon. That is today's weakness: in reel-regle-180 the first five beats are text-only cards.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Write the script as a table with these columns: t_start (in beats) | line (8 words max) | image/metaphor | persistent object | Point expression + pose + gaze target | sfx. The persistent-object column must chain: each beat's object has to transform into the next one (axis line → timeline cut → CTA underline). Store this table as timeline.json. It is the single source of truth for render(t), the numpy audio and the lint script.

quality_drivers.driver: 2. A recurring protagonist with life and reactions (Point replaces the personas)
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: The three personas keep the exact same scale and screen slots from the opener through the tunnel, the 3D room and the CTA, so they anchor the eye across radically different scenes. They have idle blinks and breathing. Maya visibly cringes when 'STICKY' tears, so the data gets a human reaction. The cast returns as an audience in the CTA. In the UI the cursor acts as the narrator and shows where to look.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Point is the single protagonist, on screen from frame 0 until it lands in the logo. It has a home slot under the title (brand board: 'toujours dans la zone visible, sous le titre') at a constant size, about 200-230 px body diameter. Use its brand-board role, 'le cobaye des astuces': Point tries the wrong way first and reacts (ennuyé + pfff), then the right way (content + tadam). Map expressions to beats: curieux = hook question, surpris = tip reveal, concentré = explanation, content = result, ennuyé = bad example, neutre = listening. Map poses: téléphone = the scrolling viewer and the CTA, il montre = points at the detail the line is about, caméra = shooting tips, salue = ending only. Point's eyes always look at what the viewer should read next. That replaces the reference's cursor-as-narrator and is already in the brand board ('ses pupilles suivent l'élément important'). Point moves between scenes by walking or jumping into the next slot instead of a cut.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Build an SVG component point({x, y, r, invert, expr, pose, gaze, t}) that is a pure function of t. Breathing: scale 1 + 0.02*sin(2*pi*t/3). Blinks: scheduled with a seeded PRNG every 3-5 s, 0.15 s close and open (scaleY on the eye ellipses). Gaze: pupil offset of at most 0.12 R toward the active element's centre, eased over 0.25 s between keyed targets. Jump: anticipation squash (scaleX 1.04 / scaleY 0.94, 0.12 s), a 0.45 s arc, landing squash 0.1 s, then settle. Squash and stretch happen only during jumps; the body is never deformed otherwise (brand rule). Add a contact-shadow ellipse whose opacity and size follow height. Limbs are round-cap strokes at the signature's stroke width. Expression changes cross-blend the eye shapes over 0.18 s. Emote glyphs '?' and '!' pop in over 0.25 s with ease-out and at most 3% overshoot. No mouth, no speech bubble, no clones of Point.

quality_drivers.driver: 3. One-take continuity: objects persist and transform, seams are hidden
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: The board tiles become the feed cells. One ad zooms out into a wall. The hero logo shrinks into the app's sidebar logo (scale match move). The grey card cracks into shards, which become thumbnails, then an orbit, then a chart. The code glyphs become the CTA confetti. A persona slot card expands into Maya's full-screen world (shared-element transition). Debris from the shatter still crosses the next scene. In segment 2 there are no hard cuts at all, and the one deliberate hard cut (problem → solution) is the emotional break.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Build each reel as one continuous world with a virtual camera. House transitions: (a) Shared element: a timeline clip thumbnail expands to full screen and becomes the scene; a viewfinder frame grows into the video frame; a browser window shrinks into the phone Point holds. (b) A camera move through the same space: pan along a long timeline, push into a monitor. (c) Point as the bridge: it jumps from one scene into the next. (d) Signature transition, at most once per video: the full stop that ends the headline (the 'point', the brand's own symbol) grows into a circular iris that reveals the inverted world (bordeaux ↔ off-white). The outgoing elements finish their motion over the incoming scene, with 0.2-0.4 s of follow-through overlap.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Give every element in the scene graph a persistent id. Implement transitions as FLIP-style interpolation of an element's rect between two layouts (x, y, w, h, radius), lerped inside render(t) with easeInOutCubic over 0.8-1.1 s. Full-stop iris: clip-path: circle(r at x y), with r going from the dot radius to hypot(1080, 1920) over 0.9 s easeInOutQuart, anchored on the measured position of the '.' glyph (use a Range on the last character and getBoundingClientRect). Allow at most one unmotivated hard cut per video, placed on a quiet sound pocket.

quality_drivers.driver: 4. Real depth and a virtual camera (in a calm register)
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: A forward dolly through about 15 rings of cards with roll and near-lens parallax. A dolly-zoom on the 3D room, where the subjects stay the same size while the corridor stretches. Cards orbit the tube with correct occlusion. The dashboard floats tilted 10-15° and eases to flat. Shards and cards fly past the lens with motion blur. A rack focus dims the clock behind the hero quote. The Maya scene has five or more parallax planes. No frame is ever a flat slide.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Keep the camera always alive but slow: a 2-4% push or drift during every hold, and real moves eased over 0.8-1.4 s. Present UI objects (timeline, viewfinder, artboard, browser) as physical objects at a 6-12° tilt that settle flat when the text needs reading. Use rack focus as the main 'change of attention': the background blurs to 6-10 px when the hero object or Point comes forward. Use four to six depth planes: background gradient → texture (dot grid, film perforations, ruler ticks) → secondary objects (blurred) → hero object → Point → very low-opacity out-of-focus foreground shapes drifting slowly. One dolly-zoom per video at most, ideal for the stakes beat ('ton spectateur décroche': the room stretches away while Point and the line stay fixed). No fast fly-throughs and no objects hurled at the lens.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: A tiny JS projection is enough. Each layer has (x, y, z) and the camera has (cx, cy, cz, f). Screen scale s = f/(z - cz) and screen position = ((x - cx)*s + 540, (y - cy)*s + 760). The vanishing point and stage centre is y = 760, the midpoint of the 270-1250 band. Blur = min(12, k*|z - focusZ|) px via CSS filter, and z-index is sorted by z each frame. Alternatively use perspective: 1400px with transform-style: preserve-3d on a stage div. Dolly-zoom: keep f/(z_subject - cz) constant while cz changes. Keep every move one-point and centred on the stage axis, as the reference does. That is what makes very different scenes feel like one space.

quality_drivers.driver: 5. Light, material and atmosphere: richness from tonal depth, not hue
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: The frame is never a flat fill. There are radial hot spots and vignettes, a warm bloom behind the characters, rim light on white objects, glass cards with 1 px light borders and inner glow, large soft drop shadows on floating UI, an anamorphic flare, star dust, and depth that darkens toward the vanishing point. Lighting changes also work as transitions: a white flash, and a sky cycle from day to night.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Get the reference's richness from value and material inside bordeaux. Background: bordeaux with a soft off-centre key light, rising to about #6F2A37 at its core, and a vignette down to #460C17. Never go to black, and only touch merlot as the rare accent. Glass panels: off-white fill at 6-10%, a 1 px off-white border at 18-24%, a 1 px top-edge highlight at 35%, and a merlot inner shadow. Shadows on bordeaux are merlot-tinted, large and soft, plus a tight contact shadow. Shadows on off-white are bordeaux at 8-14%, never grey or black. Give Point a thin off-white rim arc on the side facing the key light so it reads as a lit object. A light change (a slow exposure lift to off-white over 0.5-0.7 s) replaces the reference's two-frame white flash.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Hue-locked tokens, all at hue 348-350°: --merlot #1C0509, --b-950 #360911, --b-900 #460C17, --bordeaux #5C0F1E, --b-650 #651D2B, --b-600 #6F2A37, --b-500 #7B3D48 (small elements only), --b-400 #925F68 (strokes and labels only, never surfaces), --w-200 #E1D3D3, --w-100 #EBE1E0, --w-50 #F1EAE9, --blanc #F7F3F1. Build glows with normal blending of off-white at low alpha. Screen or plus-lighter blending on bordeaux pushes it toward raspberry red, and mixing with black or grey pushes it toward brown, which is very likely why the earlier merlot backgrounds read as 'marron'. Avoid large mid-tone surfaces: mid-mixes read as dusty mauve. Add luminance-only grain at 3-4% opacity from a seeded 540x960 noise canvas, refreshed every 2 frames, to stop banding in dark gradients.

quality_drivers.driver: 6. Colour as narrative code, rebuilt as a value and inversion code
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Each persona owns one hue that carries from card to wall to particle to bar to label. Lime is reserved for 'the insight' (the 3, the counter, the burst, the keyword). Grey means generic or 'before'. Green means connected. On the negative line 'Not yours.' the accent colour is removed. The meaning is readable with no explanation.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: With two colours, encode meaning in six ways. (1) Inversion: the bordeaux world is the problem or question, the off-white world is the answer, and Point inverts with the world. (2) Fill vs outline: solid means right or final, a dashed outline means empty, placeholder or wrong. (3) Opacity tiers: 100 / 60 / 30 for focus / secondary / context. (4) Weight: Bricolage bold for the key words, light for connective words. His established bold+light contrast replaces the reference's lime accent: one bold cluster per line. (5) Highlight block: an off-white marker wipe behind the key word on bordeaux, with the word flipping to bordeaux. This is the calm version of the magenta highlighter. (6) Merlot #1C0509 for at most one moment per video, for example the inside of the viewfinder or the stakes beat. Give each tip category a texture world instead of a hue world: video = film perforations and timeline ticks, design = dot grid and artboard guides, web = code and devtools grid.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Use semantic classes so the code reads the same in every video: .is-wrong = 2 px dashed outline at 40% plus a strike drawn on; .is-right = solid fill plus a check drawn on; .is-context = 30% opacity. Highlight wipe: a rect behind the word with scaleX 0→1 from the left, 0.45 s easeOutQuart; the word colour cross-fades over 0.15 s when the wipe passes 50%. Every inverted scene gets an inverted Point (white on bordeaux / bordeaux on white), as the brand board specifies.

quality_drivers.driver: 7. A believable micro-world: UI mockups with dense, true micro-copy
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: A complete SaaS dashboard: sidebar, KPI tiles with mono labels, timestamped reviews, '1★ RANTS', 'Sponsored · Lumen Skin', '440 × 620' dimension badges, a cursor with a click ring, and a closing code listing that names every effect. Dozens of unique review texts on the tunnel cards reward pausing and rewatching.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Draw the real tools of each topic as generic, unbranded mockups in the palette. Video tips: an editing timeline (tracks V1/V2/A1, playhead with timecode, clip thumbnails showing Point, waveform, in/out markers, razor cut) and a camera viewfinder (thirds grid, an off-white REC dot rather than red, 1/50, ISO 400, 24 fps, battery, focus box, timecode). Design tips: a canvas with guides, '1080 × 1350' badges, a layer panel and spacing redlines in bordeaux. Web tips: a browser window with a URL bar, a devtools CSS panel with real properties, and a box-model diagram. All micro-copy must be true and specific to the tip: real parameter values, real CSS, real ratios, and the reel's own running timecode. No software or Instagram logos, no fake reviews, no view counts, no client names, no handles.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Build a reusable kit/ of SVG/HTML components that take a progress parameter: Timeline, Viewfinder, Artboard, BrowserWindow, PhoneFrame, CodePanel, Ruler, Dial. Labels are Geist Mono 18-24 px with tabular numbers, at 30-60% opacity, so they add texture without competing with the headline. Target 6-12 tiny true labels per UI object. Running timecode HH:MM:SS:FF is computed from t, so it is true by construction (a diegetic match like the reference's clock = review timestamp).

quality_drivers.driver: 8. A disciplined two-voice type system and kinetic type that carries meaning
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: One heavy, tightly tracked grotesk (the analysis even names Bricolage Grotesque as the closest match) carries the human voice. A slashed-zero mono carries the machine voice (labels, data, HUD). Lines are 2-5 words in sentence case and end with full stops, so they read as verdicts. Scale contrast is extreme. Type moves according to its meaning: scramble-resolve, odometer, word-by-word blur-rise, highlighter wipe, typewriter. Every headline change uses the same roll-swap grammar.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Bricolage Grotesque for every human statement: bold condensed (wdth about 75-85, wght 700-800) on the key words, light (wght 300) on connective words in the same line. Sentence case, full stops, tracking -2 to -3%, 64-96 px, 8 words maximum, one headline on screen at a time. Geist Mono for system, HUD, labels and timecodes: 20-26 px, uppercase, tracking +8-12%, 40-70% opacity. One headline grammar for the whole video: each word rises 16-20 px, blurs from 8 to 0 px and fades in over 0.55 s easeOutExpo with a 70 ms stagger. A line exits by moving up 12 px, blurring to 6 px and fading over 0.35 s, and the next line overlaps it by 0.1 s. Choose one special type move per video: highlight wipe, typewriter inside a UI field, odometer on a true value, or a variable-font 'weight breath' on the key word (wght 300→800 over 0.5 s). The weight breath is the calm, premium replacement for slams and 3D toy letters.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Split text into word spans when building the page. Interpolate font-variation-settings ('wght', 'wdth', 'opsz' 96) inside render(t). Load fonts with @font-face from local woff2 files and await document.fonts.ready before frame 0. Reserve each word's width for its boldest state so animating the weight never reflows the line. Use font-feature-settings 'tnum' for every number. No glitch decode, no jitter and no extrusion on headlines.

quality_drivers.driver: 9. Values are animated objects that land on precise numbers
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: The counter climbs 6,158 → 10,482 with a steep expo ease-out while the headline slowly scales up. KPI counters cascade one after another. A split-flap clock ticks 5:59 → 6:00 on beat. A slot-reel age lands on '31'. An analog clock time-lapse stops exactly at 2:04 AM, the timestamp of the hero review. Bars grow segment by segment. Numbers are never static.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Animate only true values that belong to the tip: shutter 1/50, 180°, 24 fps, 9:16 or 4:5, a timecode such as 00:00:02:12, '12 images', an 8 pt grid, line-height 1.2, 150 ms. Show them as objects: a dial whose needle sweeps to 180°, a protractor arc on the axis, an odometer timecode on the playhead, a ruler measuring a margin, a frame counter on a clip. A precise number lands with credibility, and here it is also true. Never use invented performance figures.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: odometer(value): each digit is a vertical strip of Geist Mono tnum glyphs translated by the fractional part, with easeOutExpo over 0.9-1.4 s. On landing add a 2% scale settle and one soft tick. Run only one counter at a time, as a cascade like the reference's KPIs. A dial is an SVG arc with stroke-dashoffset driven by the same eased value, so the number and the needle stay in sync.

quality_drivers.driver: 10. Animation principles and easing craft (calm profile)
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Anticipation: a freeze plus crack lines before the shatter, and the counter slowing down before the hit. Follow-through: debris carries into the next scene. Overlapping action: letters land while characters rise. Staggers run 20-150 ms. Every entry has an expo or back ease-out with no linear motion. Squash and stretch on landings. Only one hero motion at a time during build phases.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Keep the principles and slow the parameters down. Entries: easeOutExpo or Quart over 0.5-0.8 s. Camera: easeInOutCubic over 0.9-1.4 s. Overshoot at most 2-3% (spring damping 0.8 or more), never a visible bounce. Small anticipation, a 3-5% counter-move for 0.12-0.2 s, before Point moves and before a transition. Staggers: 60-90 ms between words, 120-180 ms between objects. During holds there is always secondary motion (Point breathing, camera drift, a label settling), but only one hero motion at a time.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Put the named curves and a few helpers in ease.js: seg(t, t0, dur, ease) clamps to 0..1; spring(t, {freq: 2.2, damping: 0.85}) is an analytic damped spring; stagger(i, step). Ban CSS transitions, CSS animations, requestAnimationFrame and Date.now: every value must derive from t so each Playwright frame is deterministic. Particles and grain use a seeded PRNG such as mulberry32(seed + frameIndex).

quality_drivers.driver: 11. Rhythm: tension and release with readable holds, on a grid
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Events are locked to a ~161 BPM grid, with major hits about every 3 beats (~1.1 s). Each fast attack is followed by a 0.25-0.8 s readable hold. After the densest moment there is a deliberate breath (the 0.28 s 'Scrolled past.' slam is followed by an empty, calm gradient). The 11-word hero quote is held 0.8 s. The end card is held 1.65 s. The energy curve goes build → spike → silence → rebuild → calm.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Use the same architecture on a slower clock. A grid of 84-90 BPM (one beat ≈ 0.67-0.71 s), with events on half-beats. Each line is held at least 0.8 s + 0.3 s per word, rounded up to the next half-beat and counted from the moment the last word is fully in. One breath of 0.8-1.2 s with only ambient motion comes after the stakes beat, before the tip reveal. Energy curve: a calm hook with motion already running → slight tension (Point fails the wrong way) → release (the tip) → small celebration (content + tadam) → a calm CTA hold of at least 2 s. Target 30-45 s and at most 12-14 headline lines per reel.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Author timeline.json in beats and convert to seconds once. lint.js fails the render if any text hold is shorter than the formula, or if two hero motions overlap during the first 60% of a text hold. When the owner builds in Claude Design, give it the same beat table, tokens and easing values, so both pipelines share one rhythm.

quality_drivers.driver: 12. Sound locked to the picture, granular and diegetic
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Flap clatter on the scramble, a keystroke tick per typed character, thumps on word locks, whistles rising before each firework, a send sound on '✓ sent'. The stamp lands in a deliberate quiet pocket so it is felt as a low thud. Sound effects are panned by x position. A low pad sits under the outro. The prompt's own line is 'sync every tick'.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Every visible event gets a soft sound, mixed low, from one coherent family: Point's five brand sounds (bip, hm?, oh!, pfff, tadam), soft diegetic tool sounds (shutter, playhead tick, clip snap, pen on paper, key taps for the CTA) and one warm ambient bed. Leave a quiet pocket before each reveal. No marimba, no booms, no glitch noise, no voice. The full recipe is in sound_design_notes.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Generate the audio in numpy at 48 kHz from the same timeline.json the page uses, so sync is guaranteed by construction. Each sound starts 0-20 ms before its visual peak. Pan = 0.35*(2x/1080 - 1). Mux with ffmpeg as AAC 256 kbps.

quality_drivers.driver: 13. Hook: thesis, subject and protagonist in frame 0 (PVSE made invisible)
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Frame 0 already shows 'Your customers are / 3 people.' with the three characters idle-animated. Promise (this is about people), validation by contrast ('Not 10,482 reviews'), structure (three = three personas) and stakes ('You've never met them') all land inside 6 s, almost entirely through images. There is no logo or title card first. By comparison, /home/claude/hcstudio/medias/motion/reel-regle-180.mp4 spends about 15 s on five text-only cards (hook, promise, 'pourquoi ça marche', 'au programme', 'reste jusqu'au bout'), and its first diagram arrives around 18 s.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Complete PVSE within about 4 s, invisibly. Frame 0 is a full composition, and it is also the cover: the topic's hero object on stage, Point already in pose, and headline line 1 naming the subject (promise + subject together, e.g. 'Il y a une ligne invisible dans tes dialogues.'). V: during that hold Point does it the wrong way and the result visibly fails ('you do this too'). S: three dashed slots, or a mono '01 · 02 · 03' strip, appear in a HUD corner, which gives the structure without an 'au programme' card. E: line 2 states the stakes, shown with the dolly-zoom or Point's 'ennuyé'. No logo intro, no 'reste jusqu'au bout', no agenda card.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Lint checks: the hero object's layer is visible at t = 0; the topic keyword sits in a headline that is fully in by t ≤ 2.0 s; render(0) is exported as a PNG to review as the cover. Never fade in from black: Instagram autoplays from frame 0.

quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Empty dashed 'Your cast' slots and KPI tiles at 0 are set up to be filled later. 'SO sticky' is planted as the biggest pink word, then becomes the hero quote. The LUMEN tube returns as 'Lumen Skin · Amazon US'. Leo (7) returns as 'Before he runs off.' The lime '3' returns as the lime burst. The rewind recaps the whole film. The cast comes back for the CTA.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Plant three dashed slots in the hook, and fill one per tip (dashed → solid, a small check drawn on, a bip). Replay the wrong example from the hook, corrected, at the end, with the same framing (before/after split or wipe). Point's opening problem pose returns as its 'content' pose. The tip's final object becomes part of the CTA, for example the timeline clip shrinks into the phone Point holds. An optional calm recap (1.5 s or less) replaces the VHS rewind: the playhead scrubs back across a timeline whose clips are the reel's own scenes.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Keep a slots state in timeline.json. For recap thumbnails, render scene keyframes to PNG in a first pass and feed them as images to the Timeline component in the second pass, so the thumbnails are real frames of the video.

quality_drivers.driver: 15. Ending: the CTA acted out in the scene, then a living hold
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: The code glyphs become confetti. 'Comment PROMPTS' is built. The keyword is typed into a comment field at human speed, then '✓ sent', then a DM notification that shows the reward. The cast returns as an audience. The end card holds 1.65 s with ambient motion (blinks, drifting particles).
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Headline: 'Envoie-moi « MOTION » en message', with MOTION in bold. Point takes the téléphone pose and the phone screen shows a generic message field, with no Instagram branding. M-O-T-I-O-N types at human speed (6-8 characters/s) with soft key taps, then send with a bip and a small check drawn on. Point then jumps and lands in the handwritten 'hc.' as its dot (the brand's origin story as a bookend) while the signature draws on in monoline, with tadam on the landing. Hold 2-2.5 s with breathing and a slow light drift only. No fake received notification, no handles, no fireworks or confetti.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Draw the signature as an SVG path with pathLength=1 and a stroke-dashoffset draw-on over 0.8-1.0 s. Point's landing target is the dot's exact coordinates. The phone text uses the same typewriter helper as any code field.

quality_drivers.driver: 16. A filmic finish: motion blur, grain, clean encode
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Fast moves carry directional motion blur, which makes code-driven animation look shot through a lens rather than tweened in a browser. The gradients are smooth, the glows are soft, and there are no hard aliased edges.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Apply subtle motion blur only to movement faster than about 600 px/s (camera moves, Point's jump, shared-element expansions). Do not use echo or ghost trails: they read as glitchy. Keep a fine film grain throughout so the bordeaux gradients survive Instagram's re-encode without banding.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Because render(t) is pure, motion blur is the average of N sub-frame renders: N = 4-6 samples at t + i*(0.5/60)/N (a 180° shutter), accumulated in float32 with numpy, only on frames that timeline.json flags as fast. Encode: ffmpeg -framerate 60 -i f_%05d.png -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 14 -x264-params aq-mode=3 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart. Viewport 1080x1920 at deviceScaleFactor 1, PNG screenshots.

quality_drivers.driver: 17. Restraint: each effect once, and only with a reason
quality_drivers.evidence_in_reference: Glitch is used only as an in/out bookend pair. Chromatic aberration appears once, only for the REW gag. There is one deliberate hard cut, one accent colour per line, and one hero motion at a time in each build phase. The camera stays locked off whenever the elements are telling the story.
quality_drivers.how_to_apply_for_hc_studio: Effect budget per video: one signature transition (the full-stop iris), one dolly-zoom, one special type move, one merlot moment, one hard cut at most. Everything else uses the house grammar: word rise, shared element, camera push, rack focus.
quality_drivers.implementation_notes: Add a 'budget' block to timeline.json, and have lint.js count the effect types used and fail when one goes over budget.

keep_from_owner_criteria: Palette: only bordeaux #5C0F1E and off-white #F7F3F1, with dark merlot #1C0509 as a rare accent. Any tint or shade must be hue-locked (348-350°). No brown, orange, baby blue, red, pink-purple or grey surfaces, and none of the reference's magenta/lime/tangerine/navy.
Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque, bold condensed plus a light contrast in the same line; Geist Mono for labels, HUD, timecodes and values. Logo: the handwritten monoline 'hc.' signature.
Tone: premium, calm, Apple-like. No slams, shakes, glitches, whip pans or marimba blips; his rejection 'ça fait enfant, trop rapide, on arrive pas à lire' is binding.
Readability: every text held at least 0.8 s + 0.3 s per word, one headline at a time.
Hook: PVSE (promesse, validation, structure, enjeux) done invisibly, with the subject visible within the first seconds. No logo or agenda card first.
This is a tips account (video, design and web tips), not a studio. No fake stats, clients, sources, testimonials, handles or view counts.
No voice-over. Soft, pleasant sound design only.

Point, as specified in /home/claude/hcstudio/medias/mascotte/mascotte-point-brand-board.png: the dot of 'hc.' come alive. Circle body (bordeaux on white / white on bordeaux), two oval eyes with a highlight, no mouth, monoline limbs at the signature's stroke width, 6 expressions (neutre, curieux, surpris, content, concentré, ennuyé) and 4 poses (téléphone, il montre, il salue, caméra). It never speaks and has no speech bubble. It is never deformed except during a jump. It moves slowly: breathing +2% over 3 s, a 0.15 s blink every 3-5 s, eyes following the important element, soft jumps. It has 5 sounds (bip, hm?, oh!, pfff, tadam). It accompanies the text rather than replacing it, and stays in the visible zone under the title. Its role is 'le cobaye des astuces'.
Format: vertical 1080x1920. All readable content and Point stay between y 270 and 1250, so the usable stage is about 1080x980 centred at y 760. Backgrounds may bleed outside that band.

Production: HTML/SVG/CSS animated frame by frame through a pure window.render(t), Playwright screenshots at 60 fps, ffmpeg encode, numpy-synthesised sound. Or the owner builds the video in Claude Design with the same tokens and timing table.
conflicts_and_resolutions: PACE: The reference changes headline about every 1-1.5 s and packs about 6 visual ideas into 6 s (161 BPM). His rule needs 1.7 s for a 3-word line and he rejected fast cuts. RESOLUTION: copy the density in depth, not in time. Hold one line per the 0.8 + 0.3/word formula on an 84-90 BPM grid, keep the frame alive during holds (camera drift, Point breathing and gaze, labels settling, a counter landing), and allow no new text and no hero motion in the reading zone during the first 60% of a hold. A 30-45 s reel has 10-14 lines instead of about 30.

COLOUR: The reference's premium feel relies partly on a saturated four-hue palette used as a story code. RESOLUTION: never copy the hues. Replace the hue code with a value and material code: bordeaux/off-white inversion for the world switch, solid vs dashed for right vs wrong, opacity tiers, bold vs light weight for the key word, an off-white highlight block, one merlot moment, and a texture world per tip category (film/timeline for video, dot grid/artboard for design, code grid for web). Get richness from a hue-locked tonal ramp, glass, soft shadows, rim light and grain.

COLOUR DRIFT RISK: bloom, screen or additive blending and glass on bordeaux push it toward raspberry red; mixing with black or grey shadows pushes it toward brown, which is the likely cause of the rejected 'marron' backgrounds. RESOLUTION: use the precomputed hue-locked tokens only, normal-blend off-white glows, merlot-tinted shadows, and no pure black. Add a lint pass that samples frames and flags any pixel with saturation above 0.08 and value above 0.08 whose hue falls outside 335-360° or 0-10°.

HIGH-ENERGY FX: glass shatter, glitch/datamosh, sticker slam with shake, whip pan, RGB split, VHS rewind and confetti all read as 'enfant / trop rapide' for him. RESOLUTION: keep each move's narrative idea and change its energy. Shatter becomes the axis line opening like two doors over 0.8 s, or a clean split along the line revealing the layer underneath. Glitch becomes rack focus. Slam becomes a 'press' (scale 1.04→1 over 0.35 s while the shadow tightens, rotation no more than -3°). Whip pan becomes an eased 1.0 s camera pan with light sub-frame motion blur. VHS rewind becomes a calm playhead scrub back across a timeline. Confetti becomes a slow light drift.

FAKE DATA: the reference's credibility comes from invented specifics (10,482 reviews, 0.4% CTR, 3x, a store name, testimonials, an @handle DM). His account forbids fake stats, clients and sources. RESOLUTION: get the same specificity from values that are true by construction: real camera, design and CSS parameters, real ratios, and the reel's own running timecode. Mockups must be generic and unbranded, with no imitation of real software or Instagram logos.

CHARACTERS: the reference uses three human personas, each with its own colour world, game HUD and reactions. He has one mute mascot that must not be cloned, made to speak or deformed. RESOLUTION: Point is the only protagonist and plays the 'cobaye'. Plurality comes from objects (three cameras, three frames, three slots), not from extra characters. Reactions come from the eyes, the six expressions, the '?' and '!' glyphs and the five sounds, never a mouth or a bubble. Squash and stretch only during jumps.

FORMAT: the reference is a 16:9 film (character bottom-left, cards on the right). His safe band is about 1080x980 inside a 9:16 frame, with Instagram UI below it and on the right. RESOLUTION: use a vertical stack on a central axis. Mono label strip at y 290-330; headline at y 340-560 (2 lines maximum); demo stage at y 580-1080; Point's home slot at y 1000-1240, allowed to step into the stage. Side margins of 64-72 px, and keep key elements at x ≤ 936 below y 1050, where the reels action icons start. Depth layers and blurred background may bleed outside the band but carry nothing readable.

TOY 3D TYPE: extruded candy letters (MAYA, 3x, PROMPTS), a jittery 'STICKY' and fireworks are fun but childish next to his Apple-like brief. RESOLUTION: give type depth with a two-layer shadow (tight contact plus wide ambient, merlot-tinted), place it on glass, or animate the variable-font weight. Keep the 'type acts its meaning' idea through calm moves: the weight breath, a highlight wipe, a strike drawn on, a line splitting along the 180° axis.

MUSIC: the reference rides a driving 161 BPM track with hits on every onset. He wants soft, pleasant sound and no voice. RESOLUTION: use a warm ambient pad with an implied 84-90 BPM pulse, soft diegetic sound effects and Point's five sounds, all generated from the same timeline as the picture. Sync stays frame-exact but the transients are rounded, and quiet pockets take the place of impacts.

OPENING AND META: the reference opens on its thesis, not its logo, and ends on a 'made with Claude' code reveal and a comment-keyword DM automation. RESOLUTION: he already wants the subject first, so the logo only appears at the end, when Point lands in the 'hc.' signature. Do not copy the code-credit twist into every tip; keep it as a possible one-off behind-the-scenes post. The CTA stays 'Envoie-moi « MOTION » en message', acted out on Point's phone with no fake incoming notification.

PVSE VISIBILITY vs SPEED TO SUBJECT: his latest feedback is that the subject arrives too late. The current reel-regle-180 shows about 15 s of PVSE cards before the first diagram. RESOLUTION: fold P, V, S and E into the first 4 s over a scene that already shows the subject. P+subject is line 1. V is Point failing during line 1's hold. S is three dashed HUD slots, with no 'au programme' card. E is line 2 with the dolly-zoom.

LENGTH AND DENSITY: the reference is 47 s of maximal density designed to be rewatched on a laptop. RESOLUTION: aim for 30-45 s with one idea per beat, 6-12 tiny true labels per UI object for pause-worthy detail, and a 2 s calm end hold that loops cleanly.
sound_design_notes:
Generate all sound in numpy at 48 kHz stereo from the same timeline.json that drives render(t), so every sound is frame-exact by construction. Each sound starts 0-20 ms before its visual peak.

BED: a warm ambient pad, already playing at frame 0 because the video never starts from silence or black. Two slightly detuned sines or triangles per note (±4 cents), voiced low-mid (F2-C4, e.g. Fmaj9 or Dmaj9). Attack 1.5 s, release 2 s, low-pass about 1.2 kHz, slow amplitude breathing around 0.1 Hz. The chord changes only at section changes (hook → tips → payoff → CTA), and always on a beat of the 84-90 BPM grid. No drums. At most a felt pulse made by very gently gating the pad on bar lines during the tips section.

POINT'S FIVE SOUNDS (brand board):
- bip ('petit oui', validates a step): a round sine at about 660-880 Hz, 8 ms attack, ~120 ms exponential decay, 2nd harmonic at -18 dB. Used for slot fills, checks and send.
- hm? (curiosity): a soft hum gliding 220→280 Hz over 350 ms through a band-pass formant around 500 Hz.
- oh! (surprise / reveal): a quick glide 400→800 Hz over 180 ms.
- pfff (boredom, the viewer dropping off): pink-noise breath through a band-pass sweeping 2 kHz→600 Hz over 400 ms.
- tadam (success): two felted piano-like notes, e.g. G4 then C5 120 ms apart. Sine plus decaying 2nd and 3rd harmonics, gentle attack.

DIEGETIC TOOL SOUNDS (soft and low):
- Playhead or clip tick: band-passed click at 2-3 kHz, 4 ms attack, 30 ms decay.
- Clip snap: a 180 Hz wooden tock plus a faint click.
- Shutter: two filtered noise bursts 40 ms apart.
- Pen or marker draw-on: band-limited noise whose envelope follows the stroke speed.
- CTA key taps: low-passed noise at 1.5 kHz plus a 120 Hz body, randomised ±1.5 dB and ±3% pitch per tap.
- Camera moves: an 'air' swell of pink noise low-passed at about 800 Hz, its envelope copied from the camera velocity curve. It must never sit above the bed.
- Inversion / full-stop iris: a soft swell plus a faint 2-3 kHz shimmer.
- Counters: one soft tick on landing only, never per digit.
- Headlines: at most one very soft tick on the first word of a line, never per word, to avoid the 'blips' fatigue he rejected.

FORBIDDEN: marimba or mallet sounds, booms, impact hits, risers with pitch sweeps, glitch noise, whooshes louder than the bed, any voice or TTS.

SPACE AND MIX:
- Convolution reverb with a synthesised IR (stereo exponentially decaying noise, RT60 about 1.2 s, low-passed at 4 kHz, 12-18% wet) to glue everything together.
- Pan each sound by the x of its element: pan = 0.35*(2x/1080 - 1).
- Soften every transient: attack 5 ms or more, a gentle low-pass at 6-8 kHz on effects, a slight high-shelf cut above 8 kHz.
- Leave a 0.3-0.5 s quiet pocket (bed only, ducked) before the tip reveal and before the CTA. The reveal sound then lands in near silence; that is the reference's stamp-in-a-quiet-pocket trick, made gentle.
- Duck the bed 3-4 dB under Point's sounds with an envelope computed from the event list (50 ms attack, 300 ms release).
- Levels: Point's sounds slightly above the tool sounds, effects peaking around -20 to -16 dBFS, bed around -28 LUFS short-term. Master to about -14 LUFS integrated with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, measured with pyloudnorm or a two-pass ffmpeg loudnorm.
- During the final 2 s logo hold, let the pad ring out softly so the Instagram loop restarts without a jolt.
- Export as a 48 kHz WAV and mux as AAC 256 kbps.
checklist_for_every_video: Frame 0 is a complete, readable composition (it is also the cover): the topic's hero object is on stage, Point is in pose, line 1 is starting. No fade from black, no logo.
The subject is named in a headline that is fully in by 2 s, and shown visually from 0 s.
PVSE is done in about 4 s with no agenda card: P+subject (line 1), V (Point fails the wrong way during the hold), S (three dashed slots or a '01 · 02 · 03' HUD strip), E (line 2).
Every beat has one literal visual metaphor that works with the sound off and the headline hidden. No beat is just a text card with an icon.

One persistent object transforms through the video (e.g. axis line → timeline cut → CTA underline). Transitions are shared-element moves, camera moves or Point jumping; there is at most one hard cut, placed on a quiet pocket.
Point is on screen from start to end in its home slot under the title, at constant size, with breathing, 3-5 s blinks, and eyes that follow the element to read next.
Point plays the cobaye: wrong way → ennuyé + pfff, right way → content + tadam. No mouth, no bubble, no clones, deformed only during a jump.
Every headline is 8 words or fewer, Bricolage bold for the key words and light for the rest, sentence case, full stop. Labels and values are in Geist Mono with tabular numbers.
Every text hold is at least 0.8 s + 0.3 s per word, counted from the last word fully in and rounded up to the next half-beat (checked by lint).
Only one headline is on screen at a time. The same word-rise grammar is used throughout (16-20 px rise, 8→0 px blur, 0.55 s easeOutExpo, 70 ms stagger).

Only hue-locked tokens between #1C0509, #5C0F1E and #F7F3F1 are used. The frame-sampling lint finds no pixel with saturation above 0.08 outside hue 335-360° or 0-10°, so nothing brown, orange, blue or red.
Large surfaces are either bordeaux-family or off-white-family. Dusty mid-tones appear only on strokes and labels. Shadows are merlot- or bordeaux-tinted, never grey or black.
The frame has tonal depth: a key light and vignette on the background, glass with 1 px edges, soft and contact shadows, a rim light on Point, and 3-4% luminance grain.
There are 4-6 depth planes, the camera is always slowly alive (2-4% drift), real moves are eased over 0.8-1.4 s, and rack focus is used to shift attention.
UI mockups (timeline, viewfinder, artboard, browser, phone) are generic and unbranded, with 6-12 tiny true labels each. The running timecode is real.
Every number is true and intrinsic to the tip, animated as an object (odometer, dial, ruler), with one counter at a time. No invented stats, clients, sources, testimonials or handles.

Effect budget is respected: one full-stop iris, one dolly-zoom, one special type move, one merlot moment, at most one hard cut. No glitch, shake, slam, whip pan, RGB split, extruded toy type or confetti.
Easing: nothing linear except ambient drift, overshoot of 3% or less, small anticipation before Point's moves and transitions, follow-through overlap of 0.2-0.4 s.
Setup → payoff: the three slots fill one per tip, the hook's wrong example returns corrected at the end, and the final object of the tip carries into the CTA.
All readable content and Point sit between y 270 and 1250, with x ≤ 936 below y 1050 to clear the reels icons. Element bounding boxes are checked by lint at each hold.

CTA: 'Envoie-moi « MOTION » en message' is acted out on Point's phone (typed at human speed, send, bip and check). Point then lands as the dot of the 'hc.' signature drawing on, followed by a 2-2.5 s calm, living hold.

Sound: a warm bed from frame 0, Point's five sounds, soft diegetic effects, one quiet pocket before the reveal and before the CTA. No voice, no marimba, no booms. Master about -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP or lower.
Audio and picture are generated from the same timeline.json, with each sound 0-20 ms ahead of its visual peak and panned by the element's x.

Render hygiene: render(t) is pure (no CSS transitions, rAF or Date.now), PRNGs are seeded, fonts are loaded before frame 0, sub-frame motion blur is applied only to fast moves, and the encode uses libx264 crf 14 with aq-mode=3, yuv420p at 60 fps.
Total length is 30-45 s with 10-14 lines, and the energy curve follows calm hook → slight tension → release → small celebration → calm hold.
Final review: watch once at phone size with sound off (is every line readable and understandable from the image?), and once with sound (does it feel calm, premium and in sync?).
